# `.obsidian/` — what ships and why

This folder is the vault's Obsidian configuration, trimmed to what the "Long live Markdown" series actually uses. `workspace*.json` and `plugins/` are deliberately absent (they are per-machine and can hold credentials); `.gitignore` keeps them out.

## Community plugins

Obsidian installs none of these for you. On first open it will list them as missing under **Settings → Community plugins**; install each one from the plugin browser (or say yes when Obsidian offers to). Nothing in the vault breaks without them; the notes stay plain markdown.

| Plugin | Why it is here |
|---|---|
| `notebook-navigator` | The Bear-style two-pane file browser the series screenshots. The `bear-sidebar` snippet themes it; folder notes are named after their folder (`folderNoteNamePattern: {folder}`) |
| `calendar` | The daily-note calendar in the right sidebar; the capture flow lands things by date |
| `dataview` | Live tables over frontmatter (`type:`, `status:`, `lifespan:`); `Projects/Worky/Worky Dashboard.md` is built from four Dataview queries |
| `obsidian-excalidraw-plugin` | Diagrams that live in the vault as `.excalidraw` files, drawn or generated by the `create-diagram` flow |
| `obsidian-admonition` | Custom callout types beyond the built-in set; `vault.css` styles the component callouts (`[!cards]`, `[!phase]`, `[!storymap]`, …) that this makes editable |
| `callout-menu` | Right-click insert menu for callouts, so the component vocabulary in `Reference/Components.md` is one click away |

**Bases** is a core plugin, no install. `Projects/Worky/product/crew-scheduling/Crew Board.base` has a Board view (type `kanban`, grouped by `status`) and a plain Table view. The native Kanban view arrived in Obsidian 1.14 and was early access (Catalyst) when this was written; without it the Board view will not render and the Table view still works. See [Practical PKM's review](https://practicalpkm.com/kanban-review/). Limits from that review: one grouping property, cards are individual notes, no manual ordering inside a column. The `type: kanban` key in the file is a guess from the UI, not from documentation.

`code-styler` was removed on purpose: it restyles inline code, which breaks the component chips (phase states, story chips) that `vault.css` draws from `<code>`.

## Snippets

Turn them on under **Settings → Appearance → CSS snippets**. Three are enabled by default in `appearance.json`:

- `vault.css` — **required.** The components stylesheet: every custom callout in `Reference/Components.md` (cards, tickets, phases, capability matrices, story maps, terminals, figures, decision-doc questions) is plain Obsidian markdown that only *looks* right with this on.
- `bear-sidebar.css` — dark left rail for Notebook Navigator, light everywhere else.
- `highlight-shapes.css` — shape presets for highlighted text.

`views.css` styles Dataview tables, the Bases Kanban and Canvas cards. It is not enabled by default; turn it on to use it, off to remove it. Some of its selectors are marked UNVERIFIED in the file.

The rest (plus `views`) are optional reading tweaks (`code-block`, `heading-levels`, `line-width`, `sidebar-tasks`, `dashboard`, `folder-icons`, `its-frontmatter`) and two third-party snippets kept with their headers intact: `minimal-cards.css` (MIT, Stephan Ango) and `Obsidian Colored Sidebar.css` (CyanVoxel).

`appearance.json` names no community theme. The source vault runs Catppuccin; install it from **Settings → Appearance → Themes** if you want the screenshots to match exactly.

## Two traps

- Obsidian keeps snippet and theme state in memory and rewrites `appearance.json` from it. Editing that file while Obsidian is open does nothing. Quit first, or flip the switch in the UI.
- The stylesheet keys off callout *type*, not `cssclasses`, so it survives whatever plugins rewrite the view. The one exception is `cssclasses: brief`, which only hides the duplicate filename title.
